paper.title: A Piece of Chalk
paper.author: G. K. Chesterton
paper.edition: Complete essay II in Tremendous Trifles (1909), nine body paragraphs. Preserve paragraph order, omit typographical dot separators.

rights: Public-domain original text and historical English edition. Source and edition records are kept outside the visible article.

blocks.en: I remember one splendid morning, all blue and silver, in the summer holidays when I reluctantly tore myself away from the task of doing nothing in particular, and put on a hat of some sort and picked up a walking-stick, and put six very bright-coloured chalks in my pocket. I then went into the kitchen (which, along with the rest of the house, belonged to a very square and sensible old woman in a Sussex village), and asked the owner and occupant of the kitchen if she had any brown paper. She had a great deal; in fact, she had too much; and she mistook the purpose and the rationale of the existence of brown paper. She seemed to have an idea that if a person wanted brown paper he must be wanting to tie up parcels; which was the last thing I wanted to do; indeed, it is a thing which I have found to be beyond my mental capacity. Hence she dwelt very much on the varying qualities of toughness and endurance in the material. I explained to her that I only wanted to draw pictures on it, and that I did not want them to endure in the least; and that from my point of view, therefore, it was a question, not of tough consistency, but of responsive surface, a thing comparatively irrelevant in a parcel. When she understood that I wanted to draw she offered to overwhelm me with note-paper, apparently supposing that I did my notes and correspondence on old brown paper wrappers from motives of economy.
blocks.zh: 我记得暑假里有一个美好的早晨，到处是蓝色和银色。我不情愿地从‘无所事事’这项工作中抽身，戴上一顶什么样的帽子，拿起手杖，把六支颜色十分鲜艳的粉笔放进口袋。然后我走进厨房——它和整座房子一样，属于苏塞克斯村里一位极为端正、明事理的老妇人——问厨房的主人兼使用者，有没有牛皮纸。她有很多，事实上，多得过头了；但她误解了牛皮纸存在的目的与道理。她似乎以为，一个人要牛皮纸，必定是想包裹东西。这恰好是我最不想做的事；事实上，我发现这种事超出了我的智力所能胜任的范围。因此，她着重谈论这种材料在韧性和耐用程度上的种种差别。我向她解释，我只是想在上面画画，根本不想让画保存多久。所以，在我看来，要紧的不是它结实不结实，而是纸面能不能好好显色；这一点对于包裹倒比较无关紧要。她明白我要画画后，便打算拿一大堆信纸给我，显然以为我出于节俭，才在旧牛皮纸包装上记笔记和写信。

blocks.en: I then tried to explain the rather delicate logical shade, that I not only liked brown paper, but liked the quality of brownness in paper, just as I liked the quality of brownness in October woods, or in beer, or in the peat-streams of the North. Brown paper represents the primal twilight of the first toil of creation, and with a bright-coloured chalk or two you can pick out points of fire in it, sparks of gold, and blood-red, and sea-green, like the first fierce stars that sprang out of divine darkness. All this I said (in an off-hand way) to the old woman; and I put the brown paper in my pocket along with the chalks, and possibly other things. I suppose every one must have reflected how primeval and how poetical are the things that one carries in one’s pocket; the pocket-knife, for instance, the type of all human tools, the infant of the sword. Once I planned to write a book of poems entirely about the things in my pockets. But I found it would be too long; and the age of the great epics is past.
blocks.zh: 随后，我试着解释那个颇为微妙的逻辑区别：我不仅喜欢牛皮纸，而且喜欢纸的棕色本身，正如我喜欢十月树林的棕色、啤酒的棕色、北方泥炭溪流的棕色。牛皮纸象征着创世最初劳作时的原始暮色；用一两支鲜艳的粉笔，你便能从中点出火光、金色的火星、血红和海绿，就像最初那些炽烈的星星，从神圣的黑暗中跃出。我把这些都以一种随口闲谈的方式告诉了老妇人，然后把牛皮纸和粉笔，也许还有其他东西，一起塞进口袋。我想，每个人都一定想过，口袋里随身带的东西是多么原始，又多么富有诗意。比如小折刀，它是一切人类工具的典型，是剑的幼年形态。我曾打算写一本诗集，全部写口袋里的东西。但我发现，那会写得太长；而伟大史诗的时代已经过去了。

blocks.en: With my stick and my knife, my chalks and my brown paper, I went out on to the great downs. I crawled across those colossal contours that express the best quality of England, because they are at the same time soft and strong. The smoothness of them has the same meaning as the smoothness of great cart-horses, or the smoothness of the beech-tree; it declares in the teeth of our timid and cruel theories that the mighty are merciful. As my eye swept the landscape, the landscape was as kindly as any of its cottages, but for power it was like an earthquake. The villages in the immense valley were safe, one could see, for centuries; yet the lifting of the whole land was like the lifting of one enormous wave to wash them all away.
blocks.zh: 带着手杖、小刀、粉笔和牛皮纸，我走上广阔的白垩丘陵。我沿着那些巨大的轮廓慢慢爬行；它们表现了英格兰最好的品质，因为它们既柔和又强健。它们的平滑，与大挽马的平滑、山毛榉的平滑，有着同一种意味；它们迎着我们那些怯懦而残酷的理论，宣告强大者是仁慈的。目光扫过这片景色时，它像其中任何一座村舍一样亲切，论力量却如同地震。巨大山谷里的村庄，看得出来，已经安稳存在了几个世纪；可整片土地的隆起，却像一个巨浪升起，要把它们全都冲走。

blocks.en: I crossed one swell of living turf after another, looking for a place to sit down and draw. Do not, for heaven’s sake, imagine I was going to sketch from Nature. I was going to draw devils and seraphim, and blind old gods that men worshipped before the dawn of right, and saints in robes of angry crimson, and seas of strange green, and all the sacred or monstrous symbols that look so well in bright colours on brown paper. They are much better worth drawing than Nature; also they are much easier to draw. When a cow came slouching by in the field next to me, a mere artist might have drawn it; but I always get wrong in the hind legs of quadrupeds. So I drew the soul of the cow; which I saw there plainly walking before me in the sunlight; and the soul was all purple and silver, and had seven horns and the mystery that belongs to all the beasts. But though I could not with a crayon get the best out of the landscape, it does not follow that the landscape was not getting the best out of me. And this, I think, is the mistake that people make about the old poets who lived before Wordsworth, and were supposed not to care very much about Nature because they did not describe it much.
blocks.zh: 我越过一片又一片鲜活草皮形成的起伏，寻找能坐下来画画的地方。看在上天的份上，请别以为我是要写生。我想画魔鬼、炽天使、人们在正义的黎明到来之前所崇拜的盲目老神，画穿着怒红长袍的圣徒、奇异绿色的海，以及所有那些用鲜艳颜色画在牛皮纸上格外好看的神圣或怪异的象征。它们比自然更值得画，也更容易画。一头牛在我旁边的田地里慢吞吞走过时，一个纯粹的画家也许会画它；但我总是画不好四足动物的后腿。所以我画了牛的灵魂；我分明看见，它就在阳光里从面前走过。那灵魂通体紫色和银色，有七只角，还有一切野兽所共有的神秘。然而，虽然我不能用粉笔把这片风景的最好之处画出来，却不等于风景没有唤起我自身最好的部分。我认为，人们谈起华兹华斯之前的老诗人时，恰好犯了这个错误：因为他们很少描写自然，便以为他们不大关心自然。

blocks.en: They preferred writing about great men to writing about great hills; but they sat on the great hills to write it. They gave out much less about Nature, but they drank in, perhaps, much more. They painted the white robes of their holy virgins with the blinding snow, at which they had stared all day. They blazoned the shields of their paladins with the purple and gold of many heraldic sunsets. The greenness of a thousand green leaves clustered into the live green figure of Robin Hood. The blueness of a score of forgotten skies became the blue robes of the Virgin. The inspiration went in like sunbeams and came out like Apollo.
blocks.zh: 他们宁愿写伟大的人，而不是伟大的山丘；但他们坐在伟大的山丘上写那些人。他们吐露的自然少得多，吸收的自然却也许多得多。他们用整天凝视的耀眼白雪，为圣洁贞女绘出白袍；他们用许多如纹章般绚丽的落日里紫色和金色的光，装饰骑士的盾牌。千片绿叶的绿色，汇集成罗宾汉鲜活的绿色身影；许多早已被遗忘的天空的蓝色，化成圣母的蓝袍。灵感进去时像阳光，出来时像阿波罗。

blocks.en: But as I sat scrawling these silly figures on the brown paper, it began to dawn on me, to my great disgust, that I had left one chalk, and that a most exquisite and essential chalk, behind. I searched all my pockets, but I could not find any white chalk. Now, those who are acquainted with all the philosophy (nay, religion) which is typified in the art of drawing on brown paper, know that white is positive and essential. I cannot avoid remarking here upon a moral significance. One of the wise and awful truths which this brown-paper art reveals, is this, that white is a colour. It is not a mere absence of colour; it is a shining and affirmative thing, as fierce as red, as definite as black. When, so to speak, your pencil grows red-hot, it draws roses; when it grows white-hot, it draws stars. And one of the two or three defiant verities of the best religious morality, of real Christianity, for example, is exactly this same thing; the chief assertion of religious morality is that white is a colour. Virtue is not the absence of vices or the avoidance of moral dangers; virtue is a vivid and separate thing, like pain or a particular smell. Mercy does not mean not being cruel or sparing people revenge or punishment; it means a plain and positive thing like the sun, which one has either seen or not seen.
blocks.zh: 但当我坐着在牛皮纸上涂画这些傻乎乎的形象时，我渐渐发现一件极为懊恼的事：我漏带了一支粉笔，而且是一支最精妙、最不可缺少的粉笔。我搜遍所有口袋，却找不到白粉笔。熟悉牛皮纸绘画所象征的全部哲学——不，宗教——的人都知道，白色是积极的，也是必需的。我在这里忍不住要谈谈它的道德意义。这种牛皮纸艺术揭示的一项睿智而庄严的真理，就是白色也是一种颜色。它不只是颜色的缺席，而是一种闪耀、肯定的东西，像红色一样强烈，像黑色一样明确。可以这样说，当你的笔烧得通红时，它画出玫瑰；烧得白热时，它画出星星。最好的宗教道德，例如真正的基督教，所坚持的两三项不肯退让的真理之一，恰好也是同一件事：宗教道德的主要主张，就是白色是一种颜色。美德不是没有恶习，也不是避开道德危险；美德是一种鲜明而独立的事物，如同痛苦，或一种特定的气味。仁慈不只是没有残酷，也不只是免去他人的报复或惩罚；它是一种像太阳那样清楚而积极的东西，你要么见过，要么没见过。

blocks.en: Chastity does not mean abstention from sexual wrong; it means something flaming, like Joan of Arc. In a word, God paints in many colours; but He never paints so gorgeously, I had almost said so gaudily, as when He paints in white. In a sense our age has realised this fact, and expressed it in our sullen costume. For if it were really true that white was a blank and colourless thing, negative and non-committal, then white would be used instead of black and grey for the funeral dress of this pessimistic period. We should see city gentlemen in frock coats of spotless silver linen, with top hats as white as wonderful arum lilies. Which is not the case.
blocks.zh: 贞洁不意味着不犯性方面的错误，而意味着某种像圣女贞德一样燃烧着的东西。总之，上帝用许多颜色作画；但他从未画得像用白色时那样绚丽——我几乎想说，那样艳丽。从某种意义上说，我们的时代已经认识到这个事实，并通过阴郁的服装表现出来。因为如果白色真的是空白而无色的，是消极的、不作承诺的，那么这个悲观时代的丧服，就应该使用白色，而不是黑色和灰色。我们应当看到，城里的绅士穿着洁净银白亚麻布制成的长礼服，戴着像美丽马蹄莲一样白的高顶礼帽。但实际并非如此。

blocks.en: Meanwhile, I could not find my chalk.
blocks.zh: 与此同时，我仍然找不到粉笔。

blocks.en: I sat on the hill in a sort of despair. There was no town nearer than Chichester at which it was even remotely probable that there would be such a thing as an artist’s colourman. And yet, without white, my absurd little pictures would be as pointless as the world would be if there were no good people in it. I stared stupidly round, racking my brain for expedients. Then I suddenly stood up and roared with laughter, again and again, so that the cows stared at me and called a committee. Imagine a man in the Sahara regretting that he had no sand for his hour-glass. Imagine a gentleman in mid-ocean wishing that he had brought some salt water with him for his chemical experiments. I was sitting on an immense warehouse of white chalk. The landscape was made entirely out of white chalk. White chalk was piled more miles until it met the sky. I stooped and broke a piece off the rock I sat on; it did not mark so well as the shop chalks do; but it gave the effect. And I stood there in a trance of pleasure, realising that this Southern England is not only a grand peninsula, and a tradition and a civilisation; it is something even more admirable. It is a piece of chalk.
blocks.zh: 我带着某种绝望坐在山丘上。最近的城镇是奇切斯特，只有在那里，才哪怕有一点点可能找到出售画家颜料的店。然而，没有白色，我那些荒唐的小画就会像一个没有好人的世界一样，毫无意义。我呆呆地四下望着，绞尽脑汁想办法。随后，我突然站起来，一次又一次地放声大笑，弄得牛都盯着我看，仿佛召集了一个委员会。想象一个人在撒哈拉沙漠里，懊恼自己没有带沙子装进沙漏；再想象一位先生在大洋中央，希望自己带了些海水来做化学实验。我正坐在一座巨大的白垩仓库上。整片景色完全由白垩组成。白垩堆积绵延许多英里，直到与天空相接。我俯身从坐着的岩石上掰下一块；它画出的痕迹不如店里的粉笔好，但能达到效果。我站在那里，沉醉于喜悦，明白英格兰南部不仅是一座壮丽的半岛、一种传统和一种文明，它还是一种更值得赞叹的东西：它是一块粉笔。
